359283.title: The two-dimensional integer covering asymptotic conjecture
359283.source_locations: arXiv:2307.13257 main.tex Conjecture duality (line 476), Proposition upper (proved upper bound), Theorem partialpr (lower bound for standard monotone covers), Question q:cdkfractionalnew.
359283.assessment: Only the integral lower bound f(n,2,k) >= f*(k,2) n - O_k(1) remains. A naive averaging of k-covers over translates of T_2(k) loses a factor 2; no full mechanism found. No follow-up resolution found (search 2026-11-03).

359284.title: The three-dimensional covering conjecture
359284.source_locations: arXiv:2307.13257 main.tex Conjecture c:d=3 (line 859) and megaconjecture.
359284.assessment: Refutation would need either an asymptotic integral lower bound above the conjectured slope or a periodic construction beating it for some k; the authors' Gurobi data and proofs for k<=5, k=7 leave no visible finite target. Not pursued beyond reading.

351267.title: Alon–Krivelevich–Sudakov conjecture on coloring graphs with forbidden subgraphs
351267.assessment: Alon-Krivelevich-Sudakov conjecture for every F; open in general (source arXiv:2107.05595 v1-v3 treats bipartite F). Famous hard problem: source-backed open disposition only.

346730.title: The diameter-two conjecture for extremal connected induced subgraph counts
346730.source_locations: arXiv:2006.01187 main.tex: Theorem (GeneGraphs: maximal G and co-G have diameter 2 or 3), Table 1 (unique maximal graphs n=5,6,7, with G and co-G drawn), Conjecture at line 876.
346730.finding: The hypothesis eta(G)+eta(co-G) maximal is invariant under complementation, so if G is maximal so is co-G and the conjecture would force BOTH to have diameter 2. In the source's own Table 1 for n=7, the drawn complement co-G (10 edges) has diameter 3: d(t6,t7)=3 since N(t6)={t3,t4} and N(t7)={t1,t2,t5} are disjoint and t6t7 is not an edge of co-G. Independent recomputation (scripts/eta_table1_check.py): eta(G)=91, eta(co-G)=86, sum 177 = 2^7+7-1+43, diam G = 2, diam co-G = 3. Hill-climbing (scripts/eta_local.py) reaches the same maximum 43 for n=7 from 30 random starts, every time at a 10-edge graph of diameter 3 or its 11-edge complement.
346730.consequence: The literal conjecture is refuted by the source's own data at n=7 (zero-credit correction per the r95 rule). No independent-of-source counterexample is needed or credited.
346730.extra_coverage: Hill-climb maximisers (not exhaustive): n=8 best X=117 with both G and co-G of diameter 2 (16- and 12-edge graphs); n=9 best X=274, 18 edges, both diameter 2. These are heuristic only.

345015.title: Asymptotic sharpness conjecture for broadcast domination in the infinite grid
345015.source_locations: arXiv:1912.11560 maingeneratedpictures.tex Conjecture mainconj (line 302), Propositions t1bound/t2bound, Theorem densityof3broadcast (t>17).
345015.assessment: Requires exact minimal densities for all large t; the authors report impenetrable casework. No finite certificate available.

358046.title: Closed-form conjecture for the near-extremal asymptotic coefficients
358046.source_locations: arXiv:2304.05671 hazidakis1archiv.tex Conjecture con:app:ak(k-2) (line 4135); Remark rem:app:conjectures says the quickest proof route is the generating-function technique of the source's Section 2.
358046.check: The formula reproduces the printed level-4 coefficient a_{4,+-2} (checked by hand: (k-2)=2 gives (i sqrt3 a^2/(2^2 3^4))(3Q+1 -+ 12 alpha -+ 54 kappa)).
358046.assessment: The likely proof (diagonal generating functions of the transseries in the source's own variables, with a_{k,+-k} = k a^k / 6^(k-1) giving a rational diagonal) is the method the source itself names, so routine-risk is high; the formal transseries substitution into the degenerate PIII equation makes the Lean endpoint expensive.

343978.title: Gibbs's concentration conjecture for the Ulam sequence U(1,2)
343978.assessment: Gibbs concentration of the Ulam sequence modulo lambda_2; famous open, verified numerically to 10^12 terms.

343980.title: The asymptotic period conjecture for coefficients of U(1,X)
343980.assessment: Polynomial-ring Ulam analogue period conjecture (arXiv:1910.00109 v1-v2); no mechanism for the asymptotic statement.

338530.title: Periodicity conjecture for star-Kayles games
338530.source_locations: arXiv:1802.08700v1 main.tex lines 477-512: GRAPH_G game, KAYLES_n period 12, STARKAYLES_{k,n} definition, conjecture at line 511.
338530.computation: Exact Grundy recursion for spiders S(j,l) (centre with j pendant edges and one leg of l edges), cross-checked between a pure and a vectorised implementation. For every j=0..60 and l<=3000: eventually periodic with minimal period exactly 12 and pre-period <=344 (Kayles itself: period 12 from 71). Under either indexing convention of the source (star with k vertices or k leaves) this covers k<=61. Tails relative to Kayles are irregular (no XOR-constant shift), so no uniform-in-k structure was found.
338530.literal_note: 'period a multiple of 12' is automatic once periodic (12p is a period); the substantive content is eventual periodicity for every k, an infinite family statement.
338530.lean_cost: Each fixed k needs a periodicity-threshold theorem plus a few-thousand-term Grundy computation; the all-k statement has no mechanism.

376143.title: The exact-value conjecture for the two-color Hales–Jewett number
376143.source_locations: arXiv:2607.18111v1 HJNotes.tex: Definition 11 (off-diagonal HJ, partial m-lines), Theorem 12 (HJ(k,2)<=k), Lemma 13/Theorem 14 (HJ(k,2)>=k-t), Corollary (prime k), Conjecture at line 472 and Conjecture A (line 977), Question D (line 993), Table 3 (HJ(8,2)>=7, HJ(9,2)>=7, HJ(10,2)>=7, G(8,2)=G(10,2)=7).
376143.literal_check: MathDB paraphrase says 'contains a monochromatic combinatorial line' with two colours; the source's HJ(k,2) is the OFF-DIAGONAL number (red full k-line or blue 2-line of consecutive letters). Source scope governs. The diagonal reading would be false at k=3 because HJ(3;2)=4 (Hindman-Tressler), which the source itself records, so it cannot be the intended statement.
mechanism_attempts: Reduction (new to this lane): colourings that depend only on the letter-count vector N reduce the existence of a valid colouring of [k]^(k-1) to a set B of compositions of k-1 into k parts that meets every star {c + d e_j} and has at most one member on every adjacent-letter transfer line. Exact solutions found and independently re-verified for k=3,4,5,6 (k=4: all 8 count-based solutions enumerated; k=5: 83 enumerated), k=7 by local search; k=8 (3432 vectors, 3003 stars, 6468 transfer lines) NOT resolved: exact DFS (114k nodes), restart DFS, WalkSAT with and without reversal symmetry, and WalkSAT seeded at the sum-mod-8 colouring all failed within the 110 s caps (best 94 unsatisfied clauses). The lane's pure-Python CDCL could not even solve the easy k=7 instance, so no infeasibility inference is possible.
Function-form (Latin fibre) count-based colourings: exhaustive search shows NONE exist for k=4 and k=6 (they exist for k=3,5,7).
Separable potentials phi(N)=sum_j g_j(N_j) mod k with bijective star differences: exhaustively impossible for k=4 and k=6.

Dilation-invariant tilings T (+) dA = Z_M (d=1..k-1): none for k=4 with M<=40; position-dependent additive colourings over all abelian groups of order <=16 tested for k=4: none (one case timed out, recorded).
Analytic: linear sum/weighted-sum colourings are impossible for composite k (the 1-D vdW map forces T = r + kZ, which fails for gcd(d,k)>1); recorded with proof sketch in SUMMARY.
376143.coverage: count-based existence: settled YES for k<=7 (with certificates in logs), unresolved for k=8; general colourings not searched beyond k<=7 (source already covers k<=7 by SAT).
376143.lean_cost: A construction for all k would need a uniform explicit colouring (not found). A refutation at k=8 would need UNSAT of a ~2.1M-variable instance on [8]^7: infeasible in this lane and in the kernel.
376143.remaining_lemma: Either a uniform construction of a 2-colouring of [k]^(k-1) for composite k with no red k-line and no blue 2-line, or a proof that none exists for k=8. A count-based colouring of [8]^7 (3432-variable SAT instance, encoder in scripts/hj_counts.py) would give the new exact value HJ(8,2)=8 and answer Question D negatively, but is only a parameter instance, not a resolution.
376143.prior_art: Web searches 2026-11-03 found no follow-up (only the source and a 2026 talk abstract by a coauthor). Omega HEAD 2c2975d1 truncated path screen: no Hales-Jewett paths.

367510.title: The SPR-neighbor OLA distance bound for phylogenetic trees
367510.source_locations: arXiv:2503.10169 main.tex: OLA bijection theorem, Definition of OLA distance, Theorem nni-move-bound (E<=4), Conjecture conj:spr-move-bound (line 706) with heuristic.
367510.computation: Implemented the OLA code (internal node with child clades A,B labelled -max(min A, min B); verified against a restriction-based implementation on 200 random trees) and EXACT expectations over all SPR moves (prune any non-root subtree, regraft on any edge including above the root, excluding identity). Balanced trees with 4..128 leaves under natural, random and bit-reversed labellings: E d_OLA / height stays between 0.48 and 0.67 and decreases; hill-climbing over labellings of the 32-leaf balanced tree reached only 0.649. No growth beyond O(height) observed.
367510.lean_cost: A proof would need a formal OLA/SPR model and an expectation bound: high.

368883.title: Faudree–Lehel's irregularity-strength conjecture
368883.assessment: Faudree-Lehel irregularity strength conjecture; the source (arXiv:2506.14253 v1-v8) states it remains open with asymptotic validity known (Przybylo). Famous hard problem.

364104.title: Elphick–Linz–Wocjan square-sum generalization of the Bollobás–Nikiforov conjecture
364104.source_locations: arXiv:2407.19341v1 main.tex Conjecture conj:BN_general (line 122), Theorem (graphs with O(m^{1.5-eps}) triangles).
364104.computation: Screens of l=min(n+,omega) square sums: all circulants Cay(Z_n,S), 5<=n<=30 (only equality cases, max excess 0); perturbations of disjoint unions of <=omega cliques (omega=2..5) and of unions of <=omega complete omega-partite graphs; simulated annealing on 10-vertex graphs. No violation (all maxima are equality configurations). Literature: the conjecture was checked by its proposers on all graphs with <=10 vertices and named graphs <=40 vertices (survey arXiv:2305.10290); omega=2 is the Lin-Ning-Wu theorem; n+=1 reduces to Nikiforov's theorem.
364104.lean_cost: A counterexample would need exact eigenvalue/inertia certificates (moderate-high).
